Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: Elevated TLS errors for api.redwood-inference.com across multiple edge PoPs — service: inference-hosted — severity: P1. PD incident INC-2026-512. Auto-escalation enabled.
Nina T.: Acked. I'm digging in. Adding @Omar S. for handoff.
Omar S.: I'm on standby, switching to on-call. @Nina any immediate customer reports?
support-bot: Support ticket created TKT-5482 from enterprise-quantum: 'Timeouts and TLS handshake failures since 02:12 UTC' (attached sample logs).
Liam (oncall): I see spike in 526/525 errors and SNI alerts in our edge logs, primarily eu-central-1 and ap-south-1. ALB listener logs show "no certificate for SNI" for a subset of connections.
Nina T.: Fetching listener state and ACM certs now.
Nina T.: Commands: ```aws elbv2 describe-listeners --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:... --query 'Listeners[*].{Port:Port,Certs:Certificates}'``` and ```aws acm list-certificates --region us-east-1```
infra-bot: Listener dump uploaded /tmp/listeners_1769123457.json. ACM shows two active certificates: cert-main (issued 2026-02-10) and cert-rotate-2026 (issued 2026-03-01).
Omar S.: Hmm. Recent cert-rotation job ran last night to add cert-rotate-2026 then schedule gradual roll via CDN. Could some PoPs still be routing to an origin that doesn't SNI for the new cert?
Nina T.: Doing targeted TLS check from runner in eu-central: ```curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:34.210.11.7 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health``` -> returns cert for old CN: edge-legacy.example and handshake fails on SNI match.
Liam (oncall): That IP (34.210.11.7) maps to old edge alias that should have been replaced during CDN rollout. Looks like DNS alias / regional edge mapping didn't fully propagate at some PoPs.
infra-bot: Running dig from multiple vantage points... results:
- eu-central-1: 34.210.11.7 (old alias)
- eu-central-2: 54.75.120.8 (new alias)
- ap-south-1: 34.210.11.7 (old alias)
- us-west-2: 13.57.22.3 (new alias)
Nina T.: TL;DR: Mixed DNS/edge mapping causing some clients to hit nodes that present the legacy certificate (CN mismatch) -> TLS SNI error. This explains regional variance.
Omar S.: Mitigation plan: 1) Fail traffic away from PoPs serving old alias by shifting router weights for affected regions. 2) Add backup certificate (cert-main) to ALB listener so legacy alias still has matching cert. 3) Invalidate CDN caches and re-run edge mapping job with forced sync. 4) Notify customers.
Liam (oncall): I'll do the weight shift for eu and ap regions. Command: ```routerctl set-region-weight --service inference-hosted --region eu-central-1 --weight 0.2``` and similar for ap-south-1.
Liam (oncall): Weight shifts applied. Monitoring.
Nina T.: While that's running I'm adding cert-main to listener (quick add): ```aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:...:certificate/cert-main```
infra-bot: ALB listener updated, certificate list includes cert-main and cert-rotate-2026.
Omar S.: Triggering CDN invalidation to force fresh edge mapping: ```aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E12ABC --paths "/*"```
Nina T.: Invalidation submitted (ID I12345). Expected propagation ~2-4 mins. Also decreasing DNS TTL for api.redwood-inference.com from 300 -> 60 to speed up future corrections.
support-bot: Posted interim customer status update: "We’re investigating TLS handshake errors affecting some regions. Mitigation in progress; we’ll update in 15m."
Liam (oncall): Observability update: after weight shift and listener cert add, TLS error rate in eu-central dropped 38%->6% in 90s. ap-south similar. Some clients still hitting old alias but counts shrinking after invalidation.
Nina T.: Root cause hypothesis: edge mapping job partially failed during the cert rotation window leaving a subset of PoPs routing to legacy origin IPs that present a different cert (SNI mismatch). DNS TTLs were still relatively high so cached entries caused continued hits to old IPs.
Omar S.: Confirmed logs from edge-origins: old origin still receiving traffic until PoP caches expired. There are also a dozen clients using long-lived connections that didn't re-resolve IPs quickly.
Liam (oncall): Customer impact assessment: ~18% of requests in eu/ap regions experienced TLS failures between 02:10-02:24 UTC. Two enterprise tenants reported timeouts; we opened high-priority support threads with engineers on standby.
Nina T.: After CDN invalidation and weight shifts, we're seeing full recovery across all metrics by 02:28 UTC. ALB/edge logs show no further SNI mismatch errors.
Omar S.: Cleanup: 1) Revert DNS TTL to original after 24h. 2) Add a gating check in cert-rotation runbook: verify edge mapping convergence across >=95% PoPs before switching live. 3) Add monitoring alert for mixed-origin IPs for a given hostname.
Nina T.: I'll draft postmortem summary and runbook changes. Posting customer-facing follow-up now: "Root cause identified: partial edge mapping during cert rotation causing SNI mismatches. We mitigated via traffic rebalancing, cert listener update, and CDN invalidation. Service recovered; full postmortem to follow."
support-bot: Customer updates sent to affected tenants.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-512 marked acknowledged at 02:20 UTC; resolution in progress.
infra-bot: Uploads: /var/logs/edge_mapping_1769123457.log, /tmp/curl_euc_1769123500.out
Liam (oncall): I'll remain on watch for 1 hour then hand back to rotation. If no regressions we'll close PD in 30m.
Nina T.: Filing postmortem ticket PMT-2026-162, assigning to infra-cdn and cert-ops.
Incident Bot: PagerDuty event resolved (INC-2026-512) — acknowledged at 02:20 UTC, resolved at 02:29 UTC. :white_check_mark:
Omar S.: TL;DR: Partial edge mapping + cert rotation -> SNI mismatches at some PoPs -> regional TLS failures (~18% impact) -> mitigated by weight shifts, adding backup cert to listener, CDN invalidation.
Liam (oncall): Adding follow-up actions in the channel: lower DNS TTL pre-rotation, add post-rotation propagation checks, and include long-lived connection validation in CDNs smoke tests.
Nina T.: Thanks team. Closing thread once postmortem linked. :thumbsup:
